messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv_cache.evictions increased 12x in us-west-2 over the last 5m. Autoscaler bumped rope pods x3. Error rate spike on /v1/generate (5xx ~ 6%).
Mason L: I’m on it. Paging oncall (sre-oncall). Any immediate customer pages?
pagerduty-bot: Pager duty triggered: oncall -> sre-oncall. Incident priority: P1.
sre-oncall: Reading perf dashboard now. p99 latency for rope-longctx up from 180ms -> 2.1s. kv_cardinality metric shows many unique keys (NTK windows) spiked. Likely sliding-window/YaRN interaction.
Ana Q: I’m seeing continuous-batch queue lengths explode right when long-context requests arrive. KV miss rate jumped — cache filled with large NTK prefixes.
Kim S: That matches a config rollout from 1909872000 where we increased prefetch.window to 6s for better longctx throughput. Rolling longer windows + YaRN sticky routing might cause cache storm.
Mason L: Can we mitigate by reducing prefetch/window and throttling continuous batching? Suggest immediate throttle: set batcher.max_inflight_tokens=200k (temporarily) and prefetch.window_ms=1500.
Oleg V: I can hotpatch. Preparing a minimal change for dedicated rope-serving config. Will do a canary on a subset of pods.
Ana Q: Customer impact: a small set of enterprise customers on Dedicated saw 5xx and high latency. No data loss, only degraded latency. I’ve flagged affected org ids in support.
Kim S: Also consider turning off sliding-window aggregation for YaRN routes until stable. Sliding-window + NTK causing unique KV key explosion.
Mason L: Good. Oleg, when you have the rollout command paste it here. Keep canary to 10% traffic for 5m then observe.
Oleg V: Running: ```
# hotpatch canary
rwdctl deploy --service=rope --env=prod --selector=pool=us-west-2-rope-canary \
  --set=kv_prefetch.window_ms=1500 --set=batcher.max_inflight_tokens=200000 --meta=hotpatch-1909876543
```
Oleg V: Canary applied to 3 pods (rope-canary-3/4/5). Watching metrics.
Ana Q: Logs show evictions falling on canary pods: kv_evictions/s down 80% on canary. Non-canary still high.
Mason L: Good sign. Start progressive rollout to 33% if no regression in 3m. Also set a temporary rate-limit for very long NTK requests: route filter on seq_len>16k -> 10 rps.
Kim S: Adding that rule now. Command: ```
rwdctl route update --route=yaRN-longctx --set=rate_limit=10 --filter='seq_len>16000'
```
Kim S: Rule pushed. Confirmed applied.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary metrics: p50/p95/p99 improved on canary pods. KV eviction rate decreased.
Oleg V: Progressive rollout to 33% done. No new 5xx on canary traffic.
Ana Q: Noticing another hotspot: continuous batching logic backs up when KV misses are sustained. I’m setting batch backpressure threshold lower to prevent long tail. ```
# config snippet
batching:
  continuous:
    backpressure_threshold_ms: 120
    max_batch_size_tokens: 512000
```
Mason L: OK to deploy that too as part of the hotpatch. Keep observation window to 10m.
Oleg V: Deployed batching backpressure changes. 
Ana Q: After 8m observation: overall KV evictions down 75%, p99 latency trending to ~250ms. Affected customers seeing recovery (support pinged).
Kim S: I’ll open a followup to revert the prefetch.window change in config rollout history and schedule a safe increase test later with synthetic traffic. Note: root cause likely the interaction between longer prefetch windows + YaRN sliding-window route mapping creating too many unique KV keys (NTK prefixes).
Mason L: For post-incident: allocate an eval to replay longctx heavy traces against the current prefetch strategy and YaRN routing. Also add guardrails: max distinct NTK keys per route, and a circuit that auto-reduces prefetch.window when kv_evictions>threshold.
sre-oncall: Capturing incident timeline and RCA starters. Handoff to next oncall (Kim S) at 1909876600. Please include any follow-up actions in the incident tracker.
Mason L: Thanks team. Final check: any ongoing customer 5xx?
Ana Q: No new 5xx after progressive rollout. Latency cooling. Support notified customers and created incident notes.
Kim S: Taking next shift. Will run the synthetic tests and schedule remediation.
Mason L: Closing pager, leaving as mitigated. Will keep the config change as hotpatch for 24h then plan a controlled revert test. :thumbsup:
